newsitem.title: FRANCE: France does not exclude GEC role for Thomson-CSF.
newsitem.headline: France does not exclude GEC role for Thomson-CSF.

text.p: French Industry Minister Franck Borotra said Britain's General Electric Co Plc would have to link up with either Alcatel Alsthom or Lagardre Groupe to play a role in the privatisation of Thomson-CSF.

The French finance ministry had in a statement earlier on Friday declared that bids by Alcatel Alsthom and Dassault Industrie, as well as a bid by Lagardere for the company's 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF were eligible.
But it said a third bid by GEC could not be accepted due to national security interests.
Borotra said the government's decision was in line with the "cahier des charges" of bidding conditions the state had earlier laid down. But he added GEC could still play a role.

"GEC, which believes it can play an important role in this restructuring, has to approach the two candidates which have been admitted to see what kind of agreement, what kind of negotiations can take place about the place they can have in the restructuring of the European defence industry around Thomson-CSF," Borotra told LCI television in an interview.
